how: How many CH₂ groups in each drawing have two H that can differ (diastereotopic, decision 3), written by reading the structure, not by running the rule: an sp³ CH₂ only in a molecule with a stereocentre, or a ring substituent that makes its faces differ (methylcyclohexane: every ring CH₂, C4 included, has one H cis and one trans to the methyl); an =CH₂ when the other end of its double bond carries two different groups. Two H that a mirror plane swaps are enantiotopic and give one signal: the CH₂ of ethyl crotonate, (E)-hex-3-ene, ethyl diazoacetate and 1,2-pentadiene, and the ring CH₂ of ethylidenecyclohexane (the plane of its C=C).
